details: CONFIRMED by running master's and HEAD's kit_guard.py on the commands (evidence). The old pattern matched the words anywhere (`unlink` inside `unlinkSync`, `rename` inside `renameSync`, a perl call without parentheses). The new one is `\b(?:write\w*|unlink|remove|rename|rmtree|copy\w*|move)\s*\(`: `write` and `copy` got a `\w*` suffix, but unlink/remove/rename/move did not, so node's ...Sync names no longer match, and perl's paren-less `unlink '...'` never matches a call form. The guard's promise (guard-main.sh:25-28: a write to .relay/checks is refused anywhere; "a broken guard never silently allows") now fails for cases that were refused yesterday. No existing test covers them (only G3 writeFileSync in check-mark.test.sh), so the gate stayed green.
evidence: p(){ printf '%s' "$1" | python3 -I plugins/relay/lib/kit_guard.py /Users/amidman/relay | grep -v '^C '; echo "-- master:"; printf '%s' "$1" | python3 -I kg_master.py /Users/amidman/relay | grep -v '^C '; }
(HEAD printed no X row for any of the three)
git grep -n "Sync\|perl\|unlink" -- plugins/relay/tests tests | grep checks -> only check-mark.test.sh:247 (writeFileSync)
failing_case: In the main checkout of a repository with .relay/ on its default branch:
node -e "require('fs').unlinkSync('.relay/checks/a')"     master: X (refused)   HEAD: no X (allowed)
node -e "require('fs').renameSync('a','.relay/checks/a')" master: X (refused)   HEAD: no X (allowed)
perl -e "unlink '.relay/checks/a'"                         master: X (refused)   HEAD: no X (allowed)
The same pattern drives the Y rule, so `node -e "require('fs').unlinkSync('.relay/queue/x.json')"` lost its refusal too.
Should: all four stay refused; only text that names a write word without calling it is allowed.
fix_hint: Give every word the `\w*` suffix (`(?:write|unlink|remove|rename|rmtree|copy|move)\w*\s*\(`) and add a perl form for a paren-less call followed by a quoted or `$` argument (`\b(?:unlink|rename)\s+['"$]`); add the five cases to tests/test_guard_checks_inline.py.
pass_cases: 4. kinds("python3 -c \"import glob; print('.relay/checks writes', glob.glob('.relay/queue/*.json'))\"") has no "X" (the item's failing case stays fixed).
reason: tests/test_guard_checks_inline.py:34,37,40,43 pass; kit_guard.py:382 unchanged by this fix.
findings.summary: the new call-only pattern lets node unlinkSync/renameSync and perl unlink into .relay/checks or a queue item through: refused on master, allowed now
